summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of Crohn’s disease status post total colectomy and ileorectal anastomosis was admitted for diffuse abdominal pain, primarily in the epigastrium and left lower quadrant, accompanied by watery diarrhea and prior vomiting. Initial evaluation showed normal labs, a negative stool test for C. difficile and other pathogens, and a CT scan without evidence of obstruction, inflammation, or acute abdominal process. The GI team deemed a Crohn’s flare unlikely due to normal CRP and imaging. Pain was attributed to adhesions. The patient was started on oral hydromorphone and Tylenol for pain control but elected to leave the hospital against medical advice after approximately five hours, citing persistent discomfort and preference for home management. He was discharged on his baseline medications with instructions to follow up.
